item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
With regard to point #1:
Accepted that you do not find the connection strong enough to warrant cross-linking. That proposal has been retracted.

With regard to point #2:

  • The proposed edit to the Procedures is its own separate edit. That proposal has been retracted.
  • No actual proposal to edit any Addendum was made, merely a request for comment in the hopes that another user might know of a relevant location SCP or other recurring location that could be substituted and crosslinked.

Regarding the conflict-of-interest concerns, I did discuss that issue specifically, with other members of the team, and it was agreed that the proposed crosslink was relevant enough to overcome the conflict-of-interest concerns.

And lastly, your post is worded so incredibly pompously, I have a hard time taking it seriously. You're not writing a binding contract for my soul, you're proposing a link to be added to my article.

Please don't take it too seriously, I was just trying to have fun with the formatting to stave off the monotony of my actual content.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, I'm vetoing this for the following reasons:

  1. You are proposing a crosslink to an article whose - seemingly - only connection to this article is that it amplifies something too. Even the proposed wording of the crosslink is exceedingly vague.
  2. You are not only proposing edits for crosslinking purposes, but you're proposing concrete edits to the containment procedures and an addendum that absolutely nothing to do with crosslinking or wikiwalking. There will be no such edits unless I make them, or someone proposes something I can agree with (and just to be very clear: I don't in the least agree with these proposed edits.

Aside from these points, you are proposing a link to one of your own articles, which while perfectly within scope for your role as a member of the Wikiwalk Team carries with it a distinct reek of self-promotion, especially considering the very tenuous connection between the two articles. Now, I'm going to assume this wasn't a solo action and you conferred with your fellow team members, but in the future, if you want to link one of your own articles, have another member post. And lastly, your post is worded so incredibly pompously, I have a hard time taking it seriously. You're not writing a binding contract for my soul, you're proposing a link to be added to my article.

PS: In the interest of promoting wikiwalking, why not a connection to Drewbear's SCP-1979, whose workings were in fact so similar to what I delivered as the initial rewrite, that I had to edit this article hard in order to stand out more and stave off deletion.

item.content:encoded:
The article's been rewritten since you posted this (I guess you were composing this while I posted the new version).

As already stated, this is a Safe-class SCP.

I realized I'd misinterpreted the article on Object Classes, yes.

So bacteria are a problem with this thing. That makes sense, but you don't tell us to keep this thing itself sterile. No decontamination of the device prior to or following use. Just that we test it in a "specially constructed testing environment." It would help to state it's a clean room, everything going in and coming out has to be decontaminated, etc., rather than implying it by telling people not to let any foreign organisms in, and to clarify that the device itself must be kept sterile.

Dumb as it might sound, I had about six different versions of what that special testing environment was, but none of them seem to make a lot of sense. Because none of them mentioned it being sterile. *headdesk*

The "BURN IT ALL" contingency is not bad in and of itself, but with the minimal attention that's given to telling people how to avoid it, it seems a wonder this thing isn't a pile of slag by now.

True.

We test this on people because we apparently just wanna watch them wither away, instead of lab rats or guinea pigs or what have you, and ignore the fact that people are distinctly not sterile. Nor is most any living thing, but a rat bred and grown in a controlled environment would be distinctly more so than a person. Also easier to replace.

Actually, a remote drone would be easier. I guess my point didn't come across well enough. I meant to convey that SHOULD D-Class personnel be used for testing, they should not be told about 281's effects. This to make sure they didn't get any fancy ideas about what to do with a handy little time stopping device. Even if it aged them 63 years compared to the rest of us. I agree with you that I didn't phrase that too well (what a euphemism.)

This is a pretty lame redaction and doesn't add anything. This is a cop out to blackbox how the SCP functions. I don't mean paste ████ over it, though it does that. I mean that it clumsily obfuscates how it functions, which is pointless, since you go on to say that despite our belief for some unknown reason this component is the source of the timefuck, we still can't replicate the effect despite presumably being able to duplicate it in full.

Point taken. It was meant to signify the danger of someone replicating its effects. Which I contradicted later on, as you point out.

Lastly, the addendum feels like it's trying far too hard to inflate this thing's importance.

I suppose I wanted to make it more badass than "press snooze and have 9 minutes to yourself", though to be honest the idea was that the guy they found in that mountain cabin was a total conspiracy nut who got lucky. I'll edit it a bit more to show that.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
As already stated, this is a Safe-class SCP.

Additionally:

Tests are to be run only in Site-76's specially constructed testing environment for SCP-281, with special care being taken not to introduce foreign organisms. Should such an organism inadvertently be present during activation of SCP-281, personnel overseeing testing are to start the chamber's incineration sequence.

So bacteria are a problem with this thing. That makes sense, but you don't tell us to keep this thing itself sterile. No decontamination of the device prior to or following use. Just that we test it in a "specially constructed testing environment." It would help to state it's a clean room, everything going in and coming out has to be decontaminated, etc., rather than implying it by telling people not to let any foreign organisms in, and to clarify that the device itself must be kept sterile.

The "BURN IT ALL" contingency is not bad in and of itself, but with the minimal attention that's given to telling people how to avoid it, it seems a wonder this thing isn't a pile of slag by now.

Then there's this:

D-Class personnel used in testing are not to be informed on the nature of SCP-281.

We test this on people because we apparently just wanna watch them wither away, instead of lab rats or guinea pigs or what have you, and ignore the fact that people are distinctly not sterile. Nor is most any living thing, but a rat bred and grown in a controlled environment would be distinctly more so than a person. Also easier to replace.

and a [REDACTED]. Though incongruent, this last component is believed to be the primary source of SCP-281's anomalous properties.

This is a pretty lame redaction and doesn't add anything. This is a cop out to blackbox how the SCP functions. I don't mean paste ████ over it, though it does that. I mean that it clumsily obfuscates how it functions, which is pointless, since you go on to say that despite our belief for some unknown reason this component is the source of the timefuck, we still can't replicate the effect despite presumably being able to duplicate it in full. And that's fine. But it raises questions as to why we think this component is somehow integral to its anomalous function, any more so than any other part, when we have no apparent evidence of this fact besides its "incongruity." While this incongruity may certainly be strange and worthy of note, that in and of itself isn't enough to assume it's what makes the SCP function anomalously.

The only way I can think of to conclusively test that assertion is to disassemble the device and reassemble it, substituting copies of parts for all but the supposedly incongruent one, such that it's the only part from the original employed in the copy. If the copy demonstrates the same effects, we've got a winner, and we can safely classify this single component as the SCP. This would be even safer than storing the Timefuck T-1000 powered in a locker1, as it needs power to run, an isolated component can't do anything on its own, and anyone intending to use it for testing or nefarious purposes would need to assemble it first.

Lastly, the addendum feels like it's trying far too hard to inflate this thing's importance.

Footnotes
1. Which is pretty stupid, as you don't generally store guns loaded, nor bombs fused and active.

item.title: Crayne...
item.content:encoded:
"Special Containment Procedures: SCP-281 is currently contained within maximum security storage locker 18-E on level 7 of Site-76. SCP-281's lithium-ion battery pack is to remain plugged into Site-76's main power grid unless being used in testing."

That's what is done to keep it contained. It could sit there, forever, unattended. Just kept away from people. The effects are clearly documented and understood, and no extravagant procedures of any sort are required to keep it from doing anything to anything else. This is the very definition of a Safe SCP.

Its potential to be used outside of containment or following a classification has no bearing on what it's originally classified as. The page you cited is talking about there being two categories of Keters after the fact; if Keter, then this Keter/that Keter. That's not a quality that makes an object Keter in the first place.

item.content:encoded:
A few things that I dislike about this one, though the concept overall I do like.

1) This doesn't seem keter-class, as there doesn't seem to be any indication that this can't be easily contained by just putting it in a room somewhere and not touching it. Unless it somehow is able to activate itself, it seems that without the proper input it's just a big hunk of circuitry.

2) In the description, it's listed as being comprised of a laundry list of common items, and then [redacted], which is the cause of the anomalous behavior. It almost seems like a cop-out to not list what this last piece is. While on one hand it does have the whole "mystery" to it, on the other it's like describing a normal, every day object except for the [redacted] that makes it looks not normal. Maybe there's another way to of stating that there's an added piece that serves as the anomalous function?

Keter objects fall into one of two categories: those that are of immense strategic value once controlled, or those that have been deemed impossible to destroy due to the nature of the artifact.

I'll agree with you that most Keter-class objects are usually those that either can't be contained or if contained, pose a threat to the continued survival of the human race (or the planet/universe/existence etc.), but I'd say this one falls squarely in the first category outlined above.
